thread:
alice: heads up — I noticed the per-invocation widget in the cost dashboard is showing negative cache savings for some routes this morning. cc @devin_platform and @carla-ml :thinking:

ben_m: negative how? bug in the math or sampling artifact? :eyes:

alice: looks like when we sample heavy tails (session sampling=0.1) and also attribute prefetch credits, the per-invocation line can go below zero. quick snippet from the query we run:
```sql
SELECT route, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(cache_saved_tokens) as saved
FROM invocation_metrics
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 day'
GROUP BY route;
```

carla-ml: hmm that query doesn't account for amortized prefetch credits we hand out at session start. We currently subtract saved tokens but don't add amortized prefetch cost share. result: net negative savings.

devin_platform: right — the crediting model is two-stage: immediate cache hits (free) + prefetch amortization. The UI only shows first. We should avoid negative bars; worse, customers will freak out.

emily_pm: product ask: can we show both components separately? e.g., "cache hits saved" and "prefetch amortization" stacked, with a tooltip explaining the sign. Prefer not to change the underlying econ though — just UX.

frank-sre: from infra POV negative numbers also break the sparkline aggregator (we use min/mean aggregators). Might be safer to clamp at 0 for per-invocation view and keep detailed drilldown for power users.

ben_m: clamping hides legit signals. I'd rather show sign but flag it. Proposal: add a small indicator when amortized credits > saved tokens and surface the sampling rate + crediting method in the tooltip. Also add a warning badge that links to the docs page on amortization.

alice: +1 on indicator. also, the route-level routing policy (sticky vs stateless) influences how much prefetch we amortize. can we include routing policy in the drilldown table? quick mock: route, routing_policy, invocations, tokens, saved, amortized_credit, net_savings.

devin_platform: we already have routing policy in the metadata store. pulling it into the query costs negligible extra join. performance ok. We should name the column `routing_policy` and add a small legend in the UI.

carla-ml: implementation gotcha: our sampling for token-level telemetry uses hashed session id to sample 1 in N. If we compute amortized credits at session-level then sample at invocation-level, estimates can be biased. Two options: 1) switch to session-level sampling for affected metrics, 2) continue with current sampling but expose confidence intervals.

frank-sre: option 1 increases telemetry volume. We're tight on kinesis capacity this quarter. Option 2 seems operationally safer. Show 95% CI bars and a note: "estimates depend on sampling settings."

emily_pm: product prefers option 2 if we can make the CI easy to read. Also, add a toggle called "Show raw estimates" for internal teams. External customers see clamped net_savings >= 0 by default.

ben_m: for the API debate: should the console call the internal econ service to compute amortization, or do the math in the dashboard frontend? I'd vote server-side (single source of truth) and cache results per-epoch.

devin_platform: server-side already computes per-epoch rollups. I'll add an endpoint `/econ/route_savings?epoch=...&sample_rate=...` that returns {route, tokens, saved, amortized, net, ci_low, ci_high, routing_policy}. We should version it v1.1 because of the added fields.

alice: sounds good. devin, can you also add a tiny boolean `is_sampled_session_level` so UI can show the correct tooltip?

devin_platform: yep. will include `is_sampled_session_level` and `sample_rate`. planning to land PR by EOD tomorrow.

carla-ml: I'll update the telemetry docs and add math appendix showing how amortization is computed (prefetch tokens / expected session length).

frank-sre: I'll run a quick capacity calc for the extra rollup endpoint hits. If we see >10k QPS on the console, may need to add a short CDN layer or caching.

emily_pm: action items captured: (1) devin add /econ/route_savings v1.1 with new fields, (2) UI: stacked bars + CI + warning badge + clamp for external view, (3) docs: carla update, (4) infra: frank capacity check. I'll open a follow-up ticket in JIRA and link to this thread. :thumbsup: 

costbot: noted. scheduled a daily job to recompute amortized credits at midnight UTC.

alice: thanks all. small ask: can we include a quick sample payload example in the API docs? e.g.,
```json
{"route":"/chat/completions","tokens":12345,"saved":456,"amortized":300,"net":156,"ci_low":120,"ci_high":190}
```

ben_m: looks good. I'll pick up the UI mock and post it in #design later.

alice: great. closing this thread for now — will reopen if devin's PR changes the schema. :white_check_mark:"
